newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemalan government, rebels end 36-year war.
newsitem.headline: Guatemalan government, rebels end 36-year war.

text.p: Guatemala's government and marxist rebels on Sunday signed a historic treaty ending one of Latin America's longest-running and most brutal guerrilla wars.

In a glittering ceremony in the courtyard of the National Palace, leaders of the main factions of the Guatemalan National Liberation Unit (URNG) rebels and government peace negotiatiors signed the agreement that formally put an end to a 36-year conflict in which 140,000 people died.
The treaty signing was attended by President Alvaro Arzu, leaders of many Latin American countries and Spain, and a host of dignitaries from around the world.

Boutros Boutros-Ghali, outgoing secretary general of the United Nations, which brokered the negotiations, also took part and urged the world not to turn its back on the impoverished country now that it had finished the war.

Outside the palace, tens of thousands of Guatemalans cheered as the signing ceremony was broadcast on giant video screens. They included jubilant supporters of the URNG, who earlier marched on the central plaza freely chanting support for the rebel cause for the first time in their lives.
Rank-and-file members of the 1,700 strong guerrilla army were not present, however. They said they would watch the ceremony on generator-powered televisions in their makeshift mountain hideouts.
